title: Perplexity and Nvidia Match GRPO Accuracy Using 6.5x Fewer Tokens
summary:
Perplexity and Nvidia developed a new post-training technique called JOLT that allows a single artificial intelligence model to act as both teacher and student. The method uses self-distillation and reinforcement learning to train the teacher to provide feedback that the student can effectively utilize, while penalizing the teacher for deviating too far from the student's behavior. On the MATH benchmark, JOLT matched the accuracy of the GRPO method while using 6.5x fewer training tokens.

An extended version called JOLT+ incorporates outcome-based rewards for the student model and outperforms GRPO across coding, tool use, and terminal tasks. Researchers designed the system to overcome limitations found in vanilla Online Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by refining how the model learns from its own rewards and supervision signals.

selectedTweets.text:
Sharing new post-training research on self-distillation + RL (JOLT), done together with @NVIDIAAI. 

In self-distillation, the same model performs the role of both a teacher and a student. The teacher gets extra information that the student doesn't, and the student learns from feedback provided by the teacher. However, the teacher could still use shortcuts in ways the student has no way to follow.

Our proposed approach, JOLT, trains the teacher as well, to learn from rewards on its own attempts, while penalizing any drift that's far off from what the student model would do. JOLT+ further supplements JOLT by providing the student model outcome-based rewards in addition to the teacher supervision signals.

On the MATH benchmark, we found that JOLT matches GRPO with 6.5x fewer training tokens, while JOLT+ convincingly beats GRPO across math, coding, terminal tasks, and tool use benchmarks.
